title: Privileged access snapshot and decentralized evidence plan Q4 2025
content:
Purpose and high-level summary:

This doc is a working snapshot of privileged accounts across core services (console, dedicated control plane, CI runners, KMS/HSM integrations) and a practical plan to decentralize evidence collection for quarterly least-privilege recertification. The goal: reduce central SRE/security manual effort by ~60% next quarter, shorten access-review cycle from 3 weeks to under 5 business days for most teams, and ensure every privileged entitlement has machine-checkable evidence in S3/Confluence/Siem within the quarter.

Why this is different from previous recert notes:
- Focus on decentralizing evidence capture at the owning-team level (team-run attestations + automated exports) rather than central security collecting screenshots and CSVs.
- Emphasizes lightweight machine-verifiable artifacts (signed CSVs, log slices, role-binding manifests) that map directly to RBAC v2 role ids.
- Explicitly ties SIEM exports and audit-log schema to evidence items so compliance artifacts are auditable without manual transcript.

Current privileged surface (snapshot):
- Console admin group: 18 members (mix of staff and service identities). Known stale: 3 accounts flagged by last login >180d. (see SEC-1123)
- KMS admin role: 6 principals. Two are service accounts used by on-prem backup job (backup-runner-prod) and one by legacy on-prem CI.
- Dedicated control plane superuser: 4 principals (2 humans, 2 service).
- CI runner privileged tokens: ~22 tokens across repos, of which 5 are long-lived tokens (>90d) attached to service accounts.
- Emergency breakglass artifacts: 2 active; created in 2024 and 2025, both have attached post-mortem artifacts but one lacks TTL metadata.

Primary pain points observed in prior cycles: 
- Evidence inconsistency: teams submit different artifact types (screenshots, spreadsheets, emailed attestations) making automated verification brittle.
- Mapping difficulty: RBAC v1 role names vs RBAC v2 role ids mismatch in spreadsheets.
- SIEM ingestion latency: audit logs for role_changes arrive in SIEM with 1–2 day lag when routed through intermediate pipeline.
- Owner ambiguity: several roles do not have an explicit owner in the inventory; leads to manual reassignment during recert.

Proposed decentralized evidence model (practical steps):
1) Inventory canonicalization (deadline: 2025-11-15)
   - Each role in the inventory must have: role_id (rbac-v2), owner (team alias), created_at, last_modified, and a primary evidence_url.
   - Security will publish a small inventory export script (github:repo/infra#PR-742) that teams can run to fetch their roles and create a starter evidence bundle.

2) Evidence bundle spec (teams must produce one per role by deadline 2025-11-30)
   - evidence_type: one of [policy-manifest, siem-log-slice, signed-csv-attestation, terraform-state-slice]
   - evidence_file: URL to S3 or Confluence attachment
   - signer: team lead or delegated approver (name + email)
   - timestamp: ISO8601
   - rbac_role_id: exact RBAC v2 id
   - change_links: list of Jira keys or PRs that created/modified the entitlement

   NOTE: The evidence bundle is a small JSON/CSV file uploaded to our secure S3 bucket. Security provides a lightweight CLI (rbac-evidence) to mint signatures and upload.

3) SIEM linkage and export (owner: Observability/Infra; deadline: 2025-11-22)
   - Ensure audit log schema includes rbac_role_id, principal_id, action, resource, and correlation_id for change events. (See audit-log-schema-draft: confluence link in linked_artifacts.)
   - Produce a daily role-change slice per team/cookie (S3 prefix) that maps to evidence bundles. SIEM will index the slice for search and long-term retention.
   - For near-real-time recert verification, security will run a cross-check that flags role_ids without a valid evidence_url in the inventory and create automatic Jira tickets (SEC-1187) assigned to the team owner.

4) Delegated attestation cadence (recommended):
   - Teams with >5 privileged roles: monthly light attestations + quarterly full attestation
   - Teams with 1–5 roles: quarterly full attestation
   - Teams owning breakglass/infra-master roles: ad-hoc attestation after any change + quarterly review

Operational runbook snippet (how a team runs a recert cycle):
- Step 0: Run inventory-export --team <team-alias> -> get roles.csv
- Step 1: For each role, run rbac-evidence init --role-id <id> -> creates starter bundle
- Step 2: Attach artifact(s): terraform diff link or log slice (rbac-audit --slice --from 90d)
- Step 3: Approver signs: rbac-evidence sign --approver "name" --upload -> uploads to S3 and updates central inventory via API
- Step 4: Security run: check-inventory --staleness-threshold 180d -> tickets auto-created for missing evidence

Automation and minimal SRE involvement:
- The goal is to have central security perform policy enforcement and exceptions handling only. The heavy lifting (creating evidence bundles, attaching artifacts, and signing) is done by teams through the provided CLI.
- Central SRE/Observability to ensure SIEM slices and audit-log schema are delivered and that ingestion latency is within 4 hours for critical events.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Do we accept Terraform state slices as primary evidence for roles created via IaC, or do we require an additional signed attestation? (trade-off: higher automation vs separation of duties)
- What should be the retention policy for evidence bundles (1y vs 3y) for audit readiness? Compliance prefers 3y; storage cost estimate attached as linked_artifact in SEC-1123.
- How do we handle cross-account roles (roles that grant access across dedicated/private deployments)? Need mapping enforcement so evidence includes target environment.
- Breakglass TTL metadata enforcement: should creation of a breakglass require TTL at creation time? propose: yes, default 7d with extension workflow.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- (Security) Publish evidence-bundle spec + sample bundles: Aisha (2025-10-12) - DONE (draft)
- (Infra) Deliver inventory-export script and API endpoint for inventory updates: Marcus (2025-11-01)
- (Observability) Confirm SIEM export schema and lower ingestion latency to <4h for role_change events: Eric (2025-11-22)
- (Product & CS) Identify owners for ambiguous roles listed in inventory export and assign team aliases: Priya (2025-11-08)
- (Security) Run pilot with 3 teams (platform, infra, payments) to validate evidence flow and ticketing: Aisha + Marcus (pilot window: 2025-11-10 -> 2025-11-30)

Pilot metrics to measure success:
- % of roles with a valid evidence bundle in inventory (target: 90% by 2025-11-30)
- Average time to remediate missing evidence after auto-ticket (target: <5 business days)
- Reduction in central security manual hours during recert (target: -60%)

Notes and references:
- See Jira SEC-1123 for inventory cleanup tasks and estimated storage costs.
- See GitHub PR repo/infra#PR-742 for the initial inventory-export script.
- Slack thread in #sec-ops (Oct 6 2025) contains early pilot feedback from platform team.

Quick wins for next two weeks:
- Run inventory-export for top-10 owning teams and surface ambiguous owners (Marcus)
- Publish an example evidence bundle and a 5-min screen-record for how to sign and upload (Aisha)
- Add TTL field requirement to breakglass creation API (Infra)

End of working snapshot.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep evidence bundle minimal — security can always ask for extra attachments in exceptions.
- Avoid forcing teams to restructure IaC right away; accept terraform-state-slice if accompanied by change link and approver signature.
- Need legal input on retention (cc: legal@redwood.example)
summary: Working snapshot for decentralizing privileged access evidence collection ahead of the Q4 recert cycle. Contains inventory snapshot, evidence bundle spec, SIEM linkage plan, runbook steps, open questions, and action items with owners and deadlines.
